problem: Prior VLN surveys take a CV/AI-centric, single-agent view and only briefly mention collaboration, so they give no dedicated analysis of multi-robot systems (MRS), human-robot interaction (HRI), decentralized decision-making or dynamic role assignment.
motivation: Real-world deployment in healthcare, logistics and disaster response needs robots that communicate bidirectionally, resolve ambiguous instructions and coordinate as teams. VLN models are well placed to support this, but the existing literature is scattered across CV, NLP and robotics.
key_idea: A robotics-oriented survey of about 200 VLN papers that connects VLN datasets, simulators, methods and LLM-based reasoning to MRS, HRI and ambiguity resolution, and proposes future directions.
insight: The survey argues that the main gaps are unidirectional communication, ambiguity handling, single-agent focus and sim-to-real transfer. It points to LLM-based coordination (CAMON, Co-NavGPT, RoCo, SayCoNav), interactive question-asking (ELBA, ATENA, CVDN, TEACh) and hybrid communication schemes as promising building blocks. There are no experiments or ablations; the conclusions come from a qualitative synthesis of the literature.
method: Early foundations: reviews VLN datasets (R2R, RxR, REVERIE, CVDN, ALFRED, Touchdown, etc.), simulators (Matterport3D, Habitat, AI2-THOR, Gibson, iGibson) and the evaluation metrics (NE, SR, SPL, TL, OSR, CLS, nDTW, SDTW, RGS/RGSPL).

Chronological method review: groups work into initial (seq2seq, RCM, pretraining), mid-term (graph/map/memory, data augmentation, ObjectNav, sim-to-real) and latest (zero-shot LLM/VLM, VLA, video VLMs) contributions.

VLN-based MRS and HRI: covers decentralized and LLM-driven multi-robot navigation and planning (CAMON, Co-NavGPT, MCoCoNav, SayCoNav, RoCo, CoTS, TWOSTEP) and communication schemes (centralized, decentralized, hybrid).
LLMs and reasoning in VLN: covers NavGPT, DiscussNav, NavCoT, L3MVN, AO-Planner, RAG-based methods and LLM-robotics surveys.
Ambiguity: covers active information gathering, question-asking agents (ELBA, RMM, VNLA, I3L) and ambiguity/feasibility datasets (MoTIF, TEACh).
Future directions plus an appendix table of representative SoTA methods, listing evaluation metrics, datasets and drawbacks.
numbers_note: Survey paper; no original experimental results are reported.
results: There are no experiments. The paper claims to be the first survey at the intersection of CV, NLP and robotics that covers MRS, HRI and LLM reasoning in VLN, and it contrasts itself with four prior surveys (Gu 2022, Park 2023, Wu 2024, Zhang 2024). It ends with four future directions: bidirectional HRI, ambiguity resolution, decentralized multi-robot coordination with dynamic role assignment, and sim-to-real transfer.
limitations: The review is qualitative and has no unified quantitative comparison of the surveyed methods.
The claim of covering about 200 papers is not backed by a stated systematic selection protocol, and the MRS/HRI coverage draws heavily on non-VLN multi-agent LLM work.
The future directions are broad and are not validated empirically.
builds_on: Zhang et al. 2024 VLN foundation-model survey
